Imaging shows marked contrast enhancement, necrosis (14% of tumor), crossing of the midline, ependymal invasion, extensive edema (62.8%), and a thick enhancing margin (>3 mm). These features are typical of IDH-wildtype high‑grade glioma and are atypical for IDH‑mutant tumors, which tend to occur in younger patients and show less necrosis and less aggressive enhancement. No imaging clues (e.g., calcifications, homogeneous T2 signal) suggest an IDH‑mutant phenotype. Therefore the most likely IDH status is wildtype.
